name: fort-myers
label: Fort Myers Beach and Estero Bay, Florida

shelters.name: Dunbar High School
shelters.source: 3800 Edison Avenue, Fort Myers. On Lee County's list of the 14 shelters it opened for Hurricane Ian (City of Bonita Springs notice of 29 Sep 2022 and WGCU of 27 Sep 2022, which both say every one of them took pets; the county names no special-medical-needs shelter, which is a separate one you register for, so special_needs is false). Position: OpenStreetMap way 970767988. Ground: about 18.0 ft above NAVD88 in the Cache Pack's terrain (USGS 3DEP), which is good to a few tenths of a metre, against the 9 ft below which the Flood-Prone Area is traced. Checked 2026-10-23 from maps and data only; not visited. Nobody has confirmed it opens as a shelter for any future storm.

sensor_sites.label: Fort Myers Beach Pier
sensor_sites.why: On the Gulf shore where Ian's surge was highest, so it floods first. Starts from USGS Ian deployment site FLLEE03382 (instrument 10768).

sensor_sites.label: Matanzas Pass
sensor_sites.why: Inside the island on the pass, next to the pier: reads the surge as it pushes into the bay. Starts from USGS Ian deployment site FLLEE03284 (instrument 10773).

sensor_sites.label: Caloosahatchee River at the Cape Coral Fishing Pier
sensor_sites.why: North shore of the river mouth, away from Estero Bay: shows how the surge reaches Cape Coral. Starts from USGS Ian deployment site FLLEE03374 (instrument 10857 and 10858).

sensor_sites.label: Big Carlos Pass at Lovers Key
sensor_sites.why: The pass between Estero Bay and the Gulf, where the surge enters the bay. Starts from USGS Ian deployment site FLLEE03288 (instrument 10745 and 10747).

sensor_sites.label: Mullock Creek at Mullock Creek Marina
sensor_sites.why: A creek that floods from the bay, inland of the beach. Starts from USGS Ian deployment site FLLEE03287 (instrument 10861).

sensor_sites.label: Estero Bay at Coconut Point Marina
sensor_sites.why: The back of Estero Bay, where water is pushed up after the surge. Starts from USGS Ian deployment site FLLEE03289 (instrument 10855).

sensor_sites.label: Estero River at US 41
sensor_sites.why: A river mouth just above the bay, flooded from the bay and from rain. Starts from USGS Ian deployment site FLLEE03290 (instrument 10859).

sensor_sites.label: Spring Creek at US 41
sensor_sites.why: Creek above the south end of Estero Bay, on the way to Bonita Springs. Starts from USGS Ian deployment site FLLEE03292 (instrument 10849).

hub_site.label: Dunbar High School
hub_site.why: One of the Shelters Lee County opened for Hurricane Ian, about 18 ft above NAVD88, so the Hub stays dry and powered where people gather. Every sensor site is within 30 km of it.

terrain.credit: Terrain Tiles (Terrarium) on AWS Open Data; over the United States built from USGS 3DEP
